land.text: Niger, an autonomous republic within the French Community from 18 December 1958

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's French Fifth Republic shape of 1960 (8.47 M km2) still holds all of Niger (4,436 grid cells, about 1.12 M km2); Niger's own row starts in 1961. Before 1958 Niger had been the Military Territory of Niger (1904) and a distinct colony from 1922, in French West Africa (Niger page).

correction.text: Niger as drawn for 1961: the territory that 'acquired full independence on 3 August 1960'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Niger row starts in 1961 but independence was on 3 August 1960; for 1960 Cliopatria still draws Niger inside the French Fifth Republic shape, whose dossier (eu-22) must give it up.

1,178,830 km2 against the infobox's 1,267,000 km2 (no year; 'almost 1.27 million km2' of land), ratio 0.93: within a factor of two. The frontier with Nigeria 'was finalised in 1910' and the Tibesti was transferred to Chad in 1931 (both before the state); the only later change on the pages is the 2005 award of 16 Niger River islands, too small for the grid.
Identical to the 1961 shape; the page records no territorial change after 2005 (the 2023 coup changed the government, not the frontier).

region.text: Niger, formerly a colony of French West Africa and from 18 December 1958 an autonomous republic

ledger.note: 1960-08-03: Niger becomes independent. 'Niger left the French Community and acquired full independence on 3 August 1960'; the autonomous Republic of Niger had been 'officially created under the leadership of Hamani Diori' on 18 December 1958.

region.text: the riverine islands in the Niger River on the Benin frontier, 'most notably Lété Island'; 16 of them awarded to Niger

ledger.note: 2005: the International Court of Justice divides the Niger River islands. 'Since independence there were a number of disputes over the precise allocation of 24 riverine islands, most notably Lété Island'; 'in 2005 the ICJ adjudicated on the matter, awarding 16 islands to Niger and nine to Benin.' The year and the totals are the page's (which also says 24 islands, against 16+9=25); it does not say where each island lies, so the region is the river stretch near Gaya, the crossing it names, and is below the grid's resolution.

wars.name: First Tuareg Rebellion
wars.outcome: The attack on Tchintabaraden in the Agadez Region is 'seen by some as the start of the first Tuareg Rebellion (1990-1995)'; 'In April 1995 a peace deal with a Tuareg rebel group was signed.' No border change.
wars.note: The page names no ground held by the rebels, so no contest zone or rebel dossier is recorded.

wars.name: Second Tuareg Rebellion
wars.outcome: 'The north saw the outbreak of a Second Tuareg Rebellion in 2007'; 'the rebellion had ceased by 2009'. No border change.
wars.note: No ground named; see the first rebellion.

wars.name: Benin-Niger frontier dispute

zones.text: the riverine islands in the Niger River on the Benin frontier, 'most notably Lété Island'; 16 of them awarded to Niger

wars.outcome: Not a war: a dispute over 24 (or 25) islands in the Niger River, sent to the International Court of Justice in 2001 and decided in 2005 (16 to Niger, nine to Benin).
wars.note: Listed so that the reviewer can see it was considered; the ledger records the award as a gain, not a contest.

certainty.note: Colonial frontiers (the Nigerian frontier 'finalised in 1910', the Benin frontier on the Niger and Mékrou rivers confirmed by a French statute of 27 October 1938). The 24 riverine islands were undecided until the 2005 ICJ judgment; the Saharan frontiers with Algeria, Libya and Mali are not described on the pages opened.

sources.title: Niger
sources.note: Infobox area (1,267,000 km2), Niamey, 18 December 1958, 3 August 1960, 1910 and 1931 frontiers, the Tuareg rebellions, the Benin border award, coups, the Alliance of Sahel States.

sources.title: Benin-Niger border
sources.note: The Niger and Mékrou frontier, the 24 riverine islands and Lété Island, ICJ 2005: 16 islands to Niger and nine to Benin; the French statute of 27 October 1938.

notes: Republic of the Niger: Cliopatria row 'Republic of the Niger' 1961..2024 (two identical shapes), reviewed with two pages (budget 1-2). (1) The state is dated from independence on 3 August 1960; the 1960 keyframe is new and the French Fifth Republic shape of 1960 still holds Niger (eu-22 must give it up). (2) The 2005 islands award is pixel-scale: the region is the river near Gaya (the Benin-Niger border page does not locate individual islands), and the Benin dossier should carry the matching loss. (3) The Alliance of Sahel States (the page: 'In November', after the July 2023 coup, Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger formed it) is an association, not territory: proposed as an umbrella entity under counterparts_needing_dossiers. (4) The Niger page numbers the republics inconsistently (Fourth and Fifth Republic in 1999; seven constitutions by 2010) and dates the coups of 27 January 1996, 9 April 1999 (Maïnassara's assassination), February 2010 and 26 July 2023; none changes the name or the frontier, so none is a rename. (5) The Boko Haram spillover into south-eastern Niger is on the page without dates and not recorded as a war. (6) No ruler list on the page; identity.rulers omitted. (7) No gazetteer names were needed.
